---
title: "How do I draw a histogram with counts, units, mean, and median?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I draw a histogram with counts, units, mean, and median?

## Steps in RStudio

1. Make sure you have individual numeric measurements, not just category counts.

2. Choose labeled axes and a reasonable bin width.

3. Draw the histogram and annotate counts, mean, and median.

## Runnable example

```{r}
rainfall_mm <- c(0,1,1,2,3,4,4,5,6,8,9,12)
h <- hist(rainfall_mm,breaks=5,plot=FALSE)
hist(rainfall_mm,breaks=h$breaks,col="#CEE2F0",border="#244967",
     main="Rainfall observations",xlab="Rainfall (mm)",ylab="Frequency",
     ylim=c(0,max(h$counts)+3))
text(h$mids,h$counts,labels=h$counts,pos=3)
abline(v=mean(rainfall_mm),col="#215E92",lwd=2)
abline(v=median(rainfall_mm),col="#A35E20",lwd=2,lty=2)
legend("topright",legend=c("Mean","Median"),
       col=c("#215E92","#A35E20"),lty=c(1,2),bty="n")
```

## Interpret the result

Bars count observations in numerical intervals. The labeled reference lines show the mean and median; their separation may suggest skew, but inspect the underlying values.

## Check before applying to real data

Inspect the bin boundaries. The mean and median lines are reference values, not fitted distributions.
